minutes.headline: Parks Commission adopted an amended field-use policy and refused to give the treasurer full access to the MyRec database.
minutes.summary: The Commission discussed whether the Park revolving account should move from a 53D to a 53E½ fund. It adopted the amended field-use policy and voted to have the rec director produce monthly MyRec reports instead of granting the treasurer's office access. It also discussed 2021 beach staffing, beach rental policy, hunting on park land, Marshall Park planning and a skate park meeting. The meeting lasted about three hours.

votes.motion: Accept the field use policy as amended at the meeting.
Have the recreation director produce a monthly report through MyRec and not grant someone else access to that database at this point.

budget_items.what_was_said: Field use, programs, swim lessons and beach fees go into the fund created in 1984. Under 53D the balance cannot exceed a set limit at year end.
The recreation director described a 53E½ fund that does not have to be spent down, with a yearly spending limit set by approval. It can pay salaries with benefits.
The balance brought forward from FY20 was read from the accountant's email. The commission believed it had been carried forward for many years.
figures_as_heard: thirty two thousand four hundred and sixty two dollars fifty one cents

budget_items.what_was_said: The recreation director adds a percentage to vendor program fees to cover supplies and improvements.
Payments run through MyRec and Authorize.net and reports are needed for the treasurer's reconciliation.
Swim lesson beach passes provide most beach income.
A fee for private beach use was considered, possibly more than the field use fee.
A capital planning request for a feasibility study and survey was submitted. The commission has no funds of its own for a consultant.
The parks budget lines are for maintenance and salary and are not meant for planning work. Unspent funds do not roll over.

decisions.decision: Revolving fund will return as an agenda item in a meeting or so. The chair and a member will start drafting a plan and contact the town manager, aiming to be ready by February 1 for a warrant article.
Beach staff postings to go out early January, with interviews over February and March vacations, by agreement without a formal motion.
Beach private-use policy carried over at least two meetings; recreation director to survey nearby towns and draft wording.
Hunting and firearm discharge on park land held for a future meeting, possibly expanded to firearm discharge.
A member is to send Marshall Park ideas to the recreation director. Public input will be sought, for example with an open-ended form.
Next regular meeting set for January 11 at 6:30, and a skate park meeting for January 25 at 7.
DPW director will ask the facilities superintendent to check the beach building periodically over the winter.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted unanimously, by roll call, to have the recreation director produce a monthly MyRec report instead of giving the treasurer's office access to the database.
The Commission voted unanimously, by roll call, to accept the field use policy as amended at the meeting.
The Commission discussed moving the Park revolving account from a 53D to a 53E½ fund and will return to it at a meeting soon, aiming for a warrant article by February 1.
The beach private-use policy was carried over at least two meetings, and the recreation director will survey nearby towns and draft wording.
Hunting and firearm discharge on park land was held for a future meeting, and the next regular meeting and a skate park meeting were set for January.

why_it_matters: Field use and beach fees feed the Park revolving fund, so the choice of fund type decides whether the balance can carry forward and whether salaries with benefits can be paid from fees instead of the tax-supported budget.

A warrant article on the fund, if drafted in time, would be a vote residents are asked to take at Town Meeting, and the pending beach private-use and hunting rules would change who may use park land and on what terms.
